subject: general
question: 8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days. 6 men and 8 women can build the same wall in 14 days. How many more days will 1 woman take to build that wall alone compared to the number of days 1 man will take to build the wall?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Equating work efficiency: (8M + 12W) × 10 = (6M + 8W) × 14

⇒ 80M + 120W = 84M + 112W ⇒ 8W = 4M ⇒ **1M = 2W**

Efficiency ratio **M : W = 2 : 1**. Total Work = (8 × 2 + 12 × 1) × 10 = **280 units**.

Days for **1 Woman** = 280 ÷ 1 = 280 days; Days for **1 Man** = 280 ÷ 2 = 140 days.

Difference = 280 − 140 = **140 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 140 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: **8 men** and **12 women** build a wall in **10 days**.

Case 2: **6 men** and **8 women** build the wall in **14 days**.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = (M₁ × D₁) = (M₂ × D₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (8M + 12W) × 10 = (6M + 8W) × 14

⇒ 80M + 120W = 84M + 112W

⇒ 120W − 112W = 84M − 80M

⇒ 8W = 4M ⇒ **1M = 2W**

⇒ Total Work (in terms of women) = (8 × 2W + 12W) × 10 = 28W × 10 = **280W units**

⇒ Time taken by **1 woman** alone = 280W ÷ 1W = **280 days**

⇒ Time taken by **1 man** alone = 280W ÷ 2W = **140 days**

**__Additional Information__**

Work Equivalence Formula

When different groups perform the same work, use (M₁D₁H₁) / W₁ = (M₂D₂H₂) / W₂ to find the relationship between efficiencies.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If 1M = 2W, then a man is twice as efficient as a woman and takes half the time.

Combined Rate Rule

Total efficiency of a group is the sum of the individual efficiencies of all members in that group.</p
